key_insight: A high-throughput DFT search across CuI-based ternary compounds identified 58 candidate p-type transparent conductors, showing that p-type TCM design rules extend beyond delafossite oxides to halide systems.
engineering_relevance: The study expands the materials design space for transparent electrodes in transparent electronics and tandem photovoltaics by providing a screened set of stable, optically transparent, low-hole-mass candidates.
method: Minima hopping method was used to explore CuI-based ternary X–Cu–I structures.
Density functional theory screened candidates for thermodynamic stability, optical transparency, and light hole effective mass.
The results were used to test and generalize chemical modulation of the valence band design rules.
evidence_signal: From the abstract, 58 candidates were identified, including 49 previously unreported materials and 20 degenerate semiconductors; Cu2FI2 is highlighted with a calculated gap of 3.75 eV and hole effective mass of 0.262 m0.
watch_item: The reported candidates come from computational screening, so experimental synthesis, defect control, and carrier transport validation are still needed before device use.
paper_title: High-throughput computational discovery of CuI-based ternary $p$-type transparent conductors
